title: Maya Protocol - Supercharge Cardano with decentralized native cross-chain swaps

ms.promise:
The original milestone 1 as described in Ideascale is now split into Milestone 1: "Bringing EdDSA to Maya Protocol - TSS libraries" and Milestone 2: "Bringing EdDSA to Maya Protocol - MAYANode".

Why does Maya need EdDSA?
Maya Protocol currently only supports ECSDA cryptography. To support Cardano, Maya’s TSS libraries needs to support EdDSA. 
Maya Protocol controls its vaults using TSS and is secured by MAYANodes validators via GG20 TSS for all integrated chains, ensuring security and decentralization. TSS makes Maya Protocol decentralised and secure. Read more about it here: https://docs.mayaprotocol.com/deep-dive/how-it-works/eli5/what-is-threshold-signature-scheme-tss
Maya Protocol, a friendly fork of THORChain, employs the same external TSS libraries, including one based on Binance's TSS lib, all audited by Kudelski and commissioned by THORChain.

This milestone focuses on bringing EdDSA support to the ‘go-tss’ and ‘tss-lib’ TSS libraries. 

Outputs of the Milestone
The output of this milestone will be Bringing EdDSA to the two TSS libraries Maya Protocol uses.

ms.promise:
MAYANode is the open source code that is run by Maya’s nodes (MAYANodes). 
MAYANode has the code for pubkeys, handlers, managers and Bifrösts. 

Just like the TSS libraries, these files only support ECDSA. 

This milestone will make MAYANode EdDSA-compatible.
ms.criteria:
The MAYANode code is open source. Once all changes to support EdDSA in MAYANode have been merged, this milestone should be accepted.

The following changes have been made to MAYANode to make it EdDSA-compatible and will be shared in the form of merged Merge Requests (MR(‘s)): 
-Common folder. 
-Query. 
-Mayanode message, handlers, managers 
-Bifröst (Bifröst observer needs to be updated to accept transaction sending to the EdDSA key-related address).

ms.promise:
This milestone focuses on building the observer part of the Cardano Bifröst.

Each integrated chain has a "Bifröst" client that deals with the nuances of connecting to each chain. Once nodes are synced, they watch vault addresses. If they ever see an inbound transaction, they read it and convert it into a MAYAChain witness transaction. (Read more about Bifröst here: https://docs.mayaprotocol.com/deep-dive/how-it-works/technology#the-bifroest-protocol-1-way-state-pegs )
